The Education

Why Speech Therapy Billing Loses Revenue on Every Timed Code Calculation

Speech therapy billing covers speech sound treatment, language intervention, dysphagia management, cognitive-communication therapy, fluency therapy, and AAC. The complexity lies primarily in timed code billing most SLP CPT codes are time-based, and the 8-minute rule governs unit calculation per session.

The 8-minute rule states that at least 8 minutes of a timed service must be performed to bill one unit. Each additional 15 minutes adds another unit. When a patient receives multiple timed services in one visit, the total minutes are allocated across codes per the total time rule a calculation that most SLP billing teams get wrong, resulting in systematic under-billing worth $20,000 to $45,000 annually per provider.

Dysphagia billing is one of the highest-value SLP categories Modified Barium Swallow Study (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES) have separate CPT codes beyond the treatment session code. Most practices performing MBSS and FEES bill only the treatment code, missing the instrumental evaluation codes worth $150 to $300 per study.

AAC device prior authorization is the longest authorization process in SLP billing. SGD authorization requires comprehensive communication evaluation, failed alternative trial documentation, functional limitation statement, and clinical evidence per payer. Without a structured workflow, these authorizations average 4 months and frequently result in patients going without communication devices.

The Highest Per-Session Revenue Loss in Therapy Billing

The 8-Minute Rule Timed Code Undercalculation Trap

SLP timed code billing requires distributing session minutes across all services performed and the total time rule determines how many units of each code can be billed. If a patient receives 30 minutes of dysphagia treatment and 20 minutes of language treatment, the total 50 timed minutes support 3 units distributed across both codes. Getting this distribution wrong billing only the units performed per individual code, rather than applying the total time rule systematically under-bills every multi-service session.

The most common error: an SLP provides 14 minutes of therapeutic exercise and 10 minutes of language treatment. Incorrectly: zero units billed (neither service reached the 8-minute threshold independently). Correctly: total 24 timed minutes support 1 unit of the service with more time, plus residual minutes. The difference is $65 to $85 per session in revenue permanently lost multiplying across every multi-service visit, every SLP, every day.

PMEx applies the correct total time calculation to every SLP session distributing minutes across timed codes per CMS guidelines, maximizing billable units without overcoding, and capturing all revenue the clinical documentation actually supports.
